structures.overall_structure: polycrystalline single-phase low carbon steel microstructure; large light grains separated by dark grain boundaries

phases_present.morphology: large light grains separated by dark grain boundaries (polycrystalline single phase)
phases_present.grain_size: coarse grains, largest among the compared polycrystalline datasets

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: coarse grains with few boundary intersections (largest grains among the five polycrystalline datasets)

interfaces.interface_notes: Grain boundaries are the target objects of analysis; polycrystalline images comprise tightly packed grains whose boundaries are the targets, with no voids between grains and boundaries (grain and boundary classes, no background).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: public dataset [11]; resolution 1360 × 600 pixels; 16 test images; labels not provided, part of the raw images was annotated for evaluation
characterization_methods.key_findings: good imaging conditions; polycrystalline single-phase microstructure; large variation in image resolution within the dataset

computational_details.simulation_method: MatSAM (Materials Segment Anything Model), training-free segmentation based on SAM with automated structure-aware point prompt
computational_details.software_used: PyTorch 1.13.1 library; single Nvidia RTX3090 24 GB GPU
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: image category 'polycrystalline'; Canny edge detection for ROI point generation; grid points too close to ROI points (<3 pixels) removed

unmapped_findings: Table 4 (inference time per image) on LCS (1360 × 600, polycrystalline, ARI metric): Watershed 0.54 / 6.12 ms, OTSU 0.64 / 4.54 ms, Canny 0.73 / 16.48 ms, SAM 0.86 / 1850.35 ms, MatSAM 0.96 / 1926.35 ms (source: b0115, figure_unlabelled_005).

On the LCS dataset, MatSAM achieves an ARI score of 0.96 with an inference time of 1926.35 ms per image, compared to OTSU's 4.54 ms; the high accuracy comes at a higher computational cost (source: b0117).

LCS [11] is analyzed qualitatively in Fig. 6 because the public dataset does not provide released labels; MatSAM demonstrates comparable recognition performance to the original specialist method without human intervention (source: b0074, b0076).
The real-size field of view for LCS in Fig. 1 is blank ('------'); only the pixel resolution 1360 × 600 pix is given (source: figure_001).

LCS is grouped as 'boundary' type in Table 1 (together with SS, HEA, PI-2); for polycrystalline images, grain boundary masks were extracted from the segmented grain regions using a contour-finding approach (source: b0036, b0045).

MatSAM not only segments almost all grains in LCS but also accurately identifies the vast majority of incomplete and blurred grain boundaries; despite the large variation in image resolution within this dataset, MatSAM consistently outputs satisfactory results (source: b0066).

Processing/history of the LCS steel is not reported in this paper; it is a public dataset [11] whose original labels were not provided, and part of the raw images was annotated for evaluation (source: b0024).
